evidence: The hunk ends at `from pathlib import Path` and the agent confirmed `Path` appears only on the import line, a leftover from switching to the imported `_DECLARATIONS`; removed in 04ff3f7.
guidance_note: After replacing a locally built path with an imported one, run the linter's unused-import check before pushing.

narrative: A single new static test file drew one S1 unused-import finding, fixed at once; round 1 approved. Round 1 was only the re-review of that fix, and nothing in it came from the fix.
guidance_observations: An unused import reaching review means no lint pass ran before the PR was opened; a pre-push lint would have made this a one-round PR.

evidence: The original `contested = sorted(set(declared) & absent)` with `absent = frozenset(known) - {name}` lets an engine list its own name, and `listed()` then emits it twice; 1f722a0 changed the check to `absent | {name}` and fixed the test docstring that called the case harmless.
guidance_note: When writing a contradiction check over a set of names, enumerate every name the value can collide with (others and self) before writing the intersection, and do not leave a runtime-reachable case covered only by a repo-static test.

evidence: Same defect as F1, seen from models.py; the agent took the reviewer's first option (raise) over silently filtering `foreign`, which keeps the operator informed, and added `test_a_declaration_claiming_its_own_engine_refuses_to_boot`.
guidance_note: When writing a contradiction check over a set of names, enumerate every name the value can collide with (others and self) before writing the intersection.

evidence: The refactor deleted `voices._DECLARATIONS` while `tests/test_packaging.py` still named it; 1f722a0 changed the comment to `declarations._DIRECTORY`.
guidance_note: When deleting or moving a module-level symbol, grep the whole repo, comments included, for its old qualified name in the same commit.

evidence: All three tests built `served(settings_for())`, the same settings as the module-scoped `client` fixture, and the routing refusal happens before synthesis; 1f722a0 switched all three to `client` and the agent reports the suite going from 139s to 118s.
guidance_note: When adding tests to a module that has a scoped fixture for an expensive resource, use that fixture unless the test needs different settings.

evidence: The fixture set `engine_name="declared"` with `known_engines=frozenset(ENGINES)`, a state `from_env` cannot produce; 1f722a0 adds `| {"declared"}`. The agent's single-enforcer reason for skipping a `__post_init__` check holds, since `from_env` is the only production constructor.
guidance_note: When adding a field whose invariant ties it to another field, update every hand-built instance of the type in the same commit, found by grepping for the constructor.

evidence: `replace(_settings(), engine_name="stentor")` left `known_engines` without "stentor"; 1f722a0 adds it. The agent correctly says behaviour did not depend on it.
guidance_note: When adding a field whose invariant ties it to another field, update every hand-built instance of the type in the same commit, found by grepping for the constructor and for `replace(` calls.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 1f722a0 touched only models.py and tests, while `voice_aliases` returning `_read(...).get("elevenlabs", {})` unvalidated was in the original declarations.py; the agent reproduced `AttributeError` for `elevenlabs = "oops"`, confirming the premise.
guidance_note: When adding shape validation to one reader of a config file, add it to every sibling reader of the same file in the same commit.

evidence: The F5/F6 fixes corrected two hand-built Settings but not `settings_for(engine_name="named")` in test_api.py; rather than patch a third call site, the agent made `settings_for` derive `known_engines` from the winning `engine_name`.
guidance_note: When the same fixture invariant is broken at two call sites, grep for every construction site and fix the shared helper rather than patching only the instances the reviewer named.

narrative: Round 0 raised six real findings: a missing own-name guard (reported twice), a stale comment, slow tests, and two fixtures that set an impossible known_engines. The agent fixed every one correctly in 1f722a0. Round 1 found the third copy of the fixture gap (F8), which the agent closed by having the helper derive the field, and a validation gap in voice_aliases that predated review (F7). F7 alone would have forced round 2, so no round was avoidable.
guidance_observations: Two reviewer findings described the same class of gap, and the agent fixed only the named sites; sweeping for every construction site at the first fix would have removed F8.
The agent's second-time fix at the helper rather than at the call site is the better shape and should have been the first fix.

evidence: `offered.setdefault(voice.id, []).append(backend.description.engine_name)` counts each replica, so two replicas give ["piper","piper"] and a refused boot. The agent keyed on Consul service name instead of the reviewer's engine_name, which also keeps two separate piper deployments distinct, and deduplicated `_voices`.
guidance_note: When one module deliberately returns every replica, check each consumer that aggregates its output against a scaled fleet, and add a replicas>1 test fixture alongside the single-instance one.

evidence: `max(0, last.samples + shortfall)` discards an overshoot larger than the last segment, which breaks the documented sum invariant. In 971ae3f the agent clamped each boundary to `total_samples`, so the leftover cannot be negative. That beats the reviewer's spread-or-log idea.
guidance_note: When a docstring claims an invariant holds by construction, check that every clamp or `max(0, ...)` in the code cannot discard part of the quantity being conserved.

evidence: The agent reproduced it: `ELVENSPEAK_ENGINE=router ... bake` exits 2 with "ROUTER_CONSUL_URL is required". The fix is a build-only `ARG` with a `.invalid` host rather than an ENV that would persist into the image, plus a test, parametrized over ENGINES, that configures each engine from the Dockerfile.
guidance_note: When adding a leg to a build matrix, run that leg's build step (here the bake) locally before pushing.

evidence: With `engine_name="router"` the router's alias table is empty and backends receive only resolved local ids, so ElevenLabs ids fall to the fallback voice. 971ae3f's README states this outright.
guidance_note: When documenting why a new component lacks a feature its siblings have, trace a request through it end to end and state the user-visible behaviour, not only the structural reason.

evidence: One 300s `_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` governed the boot-time `_asked` calls, while discovery used 5s to fail boot fast; 971ae3f split it into `_ASKING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=5.0` and `_SPEAKING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=300.0`.
guidance_note: When a module makes requests in two lifecycle phases (boot and serving), give each phase its own timeout, matching the sibling module's boot-path value.

evidence: `response = _request(...)` ran before `chunks()` existed, which breaks the `Speech` costs-nothing-unstarted contract; 971ae3f moved the request inside the generator.
guidance_note: When implementing a lazy-generator contract, open every resource inside the generator body, and add a test that drains the generator against a live backend.

evidence: `thread.join(timeout=...)` was never followed by a liveness check; 971ae3f adds `assert not thread.is_alive()`.
guidance_note: Follow every `join(timeout=...)` with an assertion that the thread actually stopped.

evidence: The test named for aliases only registered distinct local voices and asserted `len(voices()) == 2`, which another test already covered. The agent deleted it, which the reviewer's rewrite option allowed, and moved the scoping rule into the collision test's docstring.
guidance_note: Before naming a test after a scenario, confirm the fixture can produce that scenario; a test whose body cannot reach its title should not be written.

evidence: `known_engines` is the whole registry and `engine_name` is "router", so `model_id="piper"` reaches ELSEWHERE and gets a 422. The agent documented this and deferred the behaviour change to the owning ticket 7e2.6, a defensible scope call.
guidance_note: When documenting a routing quirk, walk every branch of the classifier (served/elsewhere/unknown) for the new deployment type, not just the first surprising one.

evidence: `f"{base_url}/v1/text-to-speech/{voice.id}/stream"` interpolated an operator-supplied id unencoded; 971ae3f added `_spoken_at` with `quote(voice.id, safe="")`.
guidance_note: When building any URL from an external string, encode it, and grep the PR for every other f-string URL built the same way, discovery.py included.

evidence: Both stubs ignored `passing`, so dropping `?passing=true` would stay green. 971ae3f made both honour it and added a discovery test, but the `Registered.passing` field it added to fleet.py was never exercised (see F32).
guidance_note: When a fake must model a filter, have one shared fake implement it, and add a test that would fail if the filter were dropped, through every fake that gained the parameter.

evidence: The cleanup comment said "Two images per run" with ONNX on each; 971ae3f rewrote it for three legs. The law was cited only as a promise to keep the text short, which is not what that law governs.
guidance_note: When changing a matrix's cardinality, grep the whole file for every prose count of its entries ("both", "two", "second") and fix them all in one pass.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 971ae3f only added a `timeout` parameter, and the narrow `(URLError, TimeoutError)` catch with unguarded reads is original code. The agent found the real mechanism was the exception types, not try placement, and made `_read_json` with `(OSError, HTTPException)`. Its truncated-body test fails on the old code.
guidance_note: When promising that every transport failure becomes a typed error, catch `OSError` and `http.client.HTTPException` around the read as well as the connect, and test with a truncated body.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: `CONSUL_URL = "ROUTER_CONSUL_URL"` was original router.py code, and its absence from `_ENVIRONMENT` predates 971ae3f; 367da24 adds it. That tuple's docstring predicts exactly this omission.
guidance_note: When adding an environment setting, add it to every registry of settings in the repo (here `conftest._ENVIRONMENT`), found by grepping for an existing sibling such as `KOKORO_MODEL`.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: `return f"http://{host}:{port}"` in `_address` was original code that 971ae3f did not touch; 367da24 brackets hosts containing ':' and adds an IPv6 test.
guidance_note: When formatting a URL authority from an address field, bracket IPv6 literals.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: unguarded `base64.b64decode` and `float(end)` in speak_timed predate 971ae3f, which only clamped boundaries. 367da24 wrapped them in `(ValueError, TypeError)` but missed `OverflowError` from `round(inf)`, which F29 later found.
guidance_note: When wrapping numeric parsing of untrusted input, enumerate every exception the conversions can raise (`float`, `round`, multiply overflow), not just ValueError and TypeError.

evidence: The F9 README paragraph in 971ae3f covered only the ELSEWHERE case (`model_id: "piper"`). Declared ids like `eleven_flash_v2_5` land on UNKNOWN through a router because there is no router.toml, which the agent confirmed and documented in 367da24.
guidance_note: When documenting a classifier's behaviour for a new deployment type, walk every input class through every branch before writing the paragraph.

evidence: The F14 fix in 367da24 added the literal "ROUTER_CONSUL_URL" even though `router.CONSUL_URL` is exported and used across test_router.py; d62e592 imports the constant instead.
guidance_note: When a fix references a name its owning module exports as a constant, import the constant rather than spelling the string again.

evidence: After 971ae3f's collision message switched to `backend.remote.backend.service`, the `Description.engine_name` comment still said it was carried for collision messages; d62e592 rewrote it to name the startup log.
guidance_note: When a fix stops reading a field for one purpose, grep for the field's docstring and update any justification that named that purpose.

evidence: The F13 fix widened only remote.py's catch, while discovery `_fetch` still caught `(URLError, TimeoutError, ValueError)` under the same docstring promise; d62e592 moved `TRANSPORT_FAILURES` into discovery and shared it.
guidance_note: When widening an exception catch for one HTTP call site, grep every `urlopen` in the package and apply the same tuple from one definition.

evidence: The F12 fix updated the cleanup comment but left the matrix rationale block's "both legs" and "the second leg", which the agent admits ("I fixed one and left the other"); d62e592 rewrote it.
guidance_note: When fixing one stale count in a file, grep that file for every other count word tied to the same list before pushing.

evidence: The F10 fix encoded voice ids in remote.py, but discovery still built `/v1/health/service/{service}?passing=true` from an unencoded catalog key; d62e592 applies `quote(service, safe="")`.
guidance_note: When encoding one externally sourced path segment, grep the PR for every f-string URL and apply the same encoding.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: `_request` never sending `xi-api-key` is an original design gap, not something 367da24 introduced. The agent added `ROUTER_BACKEND_API_KEY` as a separate setting, sent it on boot and synthesis requests, and tested both the key and no-key cases.
guidance_note: When building a client for a service that has an auth setting, design how the client presents credentials before the first push.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the sequential `_fleet` is original code. The loop is sequential, but the agent's arithmetic (7 requests x 5s = ~35s worst case against a 5-minute healthy_deadline) shows no present harm, and it filed 7e2.16 with the threshold.

Same concern as F24 one layer down, in the original discovery loop. The bounded worst case sits well inside the deployment deadline, and the reviewer's own example lists `elvenspeak-router`, which the agent says is untagged; the packet cannot confirm that, but the conclusion holds either way.

`test_a_deployment_scaled_to_two_replicas_is_not_a_collision`, added in 971ae3f for F1, called `speak(...).sample_rate` after the `with cluster` block. The same commit made speak lazy (F6), so the assertion made no request; d10eef3 drains the audio inside the block.
guidance_note: When a fix makes a call lazy, sweep the tests touched by the same commit for assertions that read only eager metadata, and drain the generator inside the resource's lifetime.

evidence: The guarded-fleet test added by the F23 fix in d62e592 asserted `speak(...).sample_rate`, the constant WIRE_RATE, so the guarded /stream request never ran. d10eef3 drains it, and the agent swept every `speak(` in the suite.
guidance_note: When writing a test for a header on a lazy streaming path, assert on drained output, and mutation-check by removing the header from that path.

evidence: The F23 fix added `BACKEND_API_KEY` without adding it to `_ENVIRONMENT`, the exact gap F14 had just named. Besides adding the entry, d10eef3 adds an AST-walking test that fails for any setting read but not cleared.
guidance_note: After a reviewer catches a forgotten registry entry once, replace the hand-maintained list with a derived check in that same fix, instead of waiting for the second miss.

evidence: The F16 fix in 367da24 caught `(ValueError, TypeError)`, but `round(float('inf'))` raises OverflowError, reachable through a JSON `Infinity` token or a multiply overflow. The agent found its first test vacuous because FastAPI returned a 500, then rewrote it to send raw bytes.
guidance_note: When wrapping numeric conversion of untrusted input, list the exceptions every operation in the chain can raise (`round` raises OverflowError on inf) and test with inf and NaN inputs.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: d10eef3 did not touch fleet.py, and the two hand-written Consul fakes existed in round 0. The F11 fix duplicated the passing filter into both instead of unifying them, which is the evidence the reviewer cites. 462ab2c merges them into one `consul_app`.
guidance_note: When a fix has to make the same edit in two fakes of one contract, merge the fakes in that fix rather than editing both.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the untested `isinstance` branches in `_tagged_services` and `engines()` are original discovery.py code that d10eef3 did not touch; 462ab2c adds a wrong-shape test.
guidance_note: When writing a parser that raises on a malformed shape, add one test per raise branch in the same commit.

evidence: The F11 fix in 971ae3f added `Registered.passing` with a comment claiming it guards `?passing=true`, but nothing set it to False; 462ab2c adds a router-level test that boots against one healthy and one failing replica.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a fixture knob whose comment claims it protects a regression, add the test that turns the knob in the same commit.

narrative: A large new router engine drew 12 mostly real round-0 findings, and the agent's fixes were generally better-shaped than the reviewer's suggestions. Those fixes then generated much of the later review: 11 of the 20 findings after round 0 trace to an earlier fix. They were missed sibling instances (encoding, transport catch, stale counts), drifted comments, vacuous tests left by making speak lazy, and fixture knobs nothing used. Every round-3 finding was fix-caused, so round 4, and the unreviewed round 5 that hit the review cap, would not have happened had the round-0 to round-2 fixes swept their class. The agent's pushback on the two concurrency findings was sound and recorded on a ticket.
guidance_observations: Each fix handled the instance the reviewer named and stopped there; a grep for the same pattern across the PR (URL f-strings, urlopen catches, count words, settings registries) at fix time would have removed F18, F20, F21, F22 and F28.
Making `speak` lazy (F6) silently hollowed out two tests that read only `sample_rate`; a behaviour change to a contract should be followed by a sweep of the tests that assert on it.
New tests written inside fixes (F26, F27, F29's first draft) were vacuous until the reviewer or the agent checked them; a mutation check on each new test before pushing would have caught them.
The PR hit the 5-round cap, so its head commit merged with round 5 unreviewed.
